templates.description:
15 min, Mon-Sat. Cards come from one source: what I built or
broke — every failure mode, every gotcha from ladder rungs and
platform Saturdays becomes a card.

In practice this is ONE sitting with the devops-ready cert deck
(07:15-07:45 back-to-back) — two templates, one habit. (A shared
common-task is specced in specs/common-tasks.md but not built.)

Add 3-5 new cards per day. No more. Crunch week? This survives.
templates.title: Anki review — build deck (15 min)

templates.description:
1st of the month: publish the ship log. Not a portfolio polish
exercise — a factual list of what went LIVE this month on the
booking platform: endpoints shipped, infra stood up, gates passed,
incidents survived.

Format:
- What users (or test users) can do now that they couldn't last month
- Exam gates passed this month
- One thing that broke and what it taught
- Link to the deployed thing

Publish wherever the senior engineers and future employers will
see it (blog / LinkedIn / repo CHANGELOG — pick one and stick to it).
templates.title: Ship log — what went live in 2026-06

templates.description:
60-90 min on the current rung's chosen challenge (see the rung
brief task — if this is the rung's first session, spend the first
15 min picking one of its 3 options and noting why in the ADR).
ADR before code. The problems you hit here are what pull reading
and feed Anki.

AI assist rule: Claude may list options or point at docs. Stuck >30 min → ask for a hint, never the solution. Claude does not write the code in this slot.

Close every session by asking Claude: 'What did I just build that has a known failure mode?' Add the answer to Friday's dive-deeper list.

Crunch week? This session + Anki + Sunday review is the whole week.
templates.title: Ladder session — Rung CLI craft & tests (60-90 min)

templates.description:
45 min, flexible slot — scheduled Monday by default; move it in
Todoist to whenever the senior engineers can make it this week.

Present the week's platform ADR/RFC (written in the Saturday deep
block). Take notes on every objection — objections are pull-reading
triggers and Anki material. An approved RFC counts toward Exam
gate 5 (log it in the Sunday state review). Owner arranges the
humans; /ladder-review is the fallback reviewer, advisory only.
templates.title: Design review with senior engineers (45 min)

templates.description:
Concept: small sharp tools; parsing; table-driven tests; clean errors.
Pick ONE — read all three briefs first:
A. [Expression calculator CLI](https://github.com/SauravSuresh/long-way-engine/blob/main/curricula/marketplace-builder/briefs/rung-01a-expression-calculator.md)
B. [Markdown -> HTML converter](https://github.com/SauravSuresh/long-way-engine/blob/main/curricula/marketplace-builder/briefs/rung-01b-markdown-to-html.md)
C. [Flashcard drill CLI](https://github.com/SauravSuresh/long-way-engine/blob/main/curricula/marketplace-builder/briefs/rung-01c-flashcard-drill.md)
Run `lw rung start` to pick and scaffold.
templates.title: Rung 1: CLI craft & tests (~2 wk) — pick one of 3

templates.description:
10–15 min. Review AWS services, K8s concepts, LeetCode patterns, and
system design principles. Add 3–5 new cards daily from what you learned
in Udemy courses and hands-on work.

Card categories:
- AWS services & use cases
- Kubernetes objects & commands
- Data structures & algorithms
- System design patterns
templates.title: Anki review (AWS/K8s/Interview prep)

templates.description:
60–90 min deep session. Watch/read, take notes in Obsidian/Notion,
then make Anki cards for the key concepts. Focus on understanding,
not just watching. Current course: Ultimate AWS Certified Solutions Architect Associate (Udemy).
templates.title: Morning study (long session): Ultimate AWS Certified Solutions Architect Associate (Udemy)

templates.description:
1st of the month: Push your completed project to GitHub with a
comprehensive README and documentation.

Project should include:
- Clear problem statement & solution overview
- Architecture diagram
- Setup/deployment instructions
- Technology stack explanation
- Screenshots/demo video
- Lessons learned section
- Link to live deployment (if applicable)

Share on LinkedIn with:
- What you built
- Technologies used
- Key challenges overcome
- What you learned

Tag: #DevOps #AWS #Kubernetes #CloudEngineering
templates.title: Publish GitHub project for Cloud Foundations & AWS

templates.description:
Continue your boot.dev backend path. Work through the current course
module, complete exercises, and build the projects. This is your
structured evening "doing" time for backend fundamentals.

Track progress in the course platform. When you complete a major
milestone (finish a course, complete a project), mark it in your
weekly state review.
templates.title: boot.dev backend path session

templates.description:
Focus on one pattern. Do 3-4 problems of the same pattern, then write
it up in your notes: when to use it, template code, common variations,
time/space complexity.

Pattern rotation (roughly): Arrays & Hashing, Two Pointers & Sliding
Window, Stack & Queue, Binary Search & Trees, Graphs (DFS/BFS),
Dynamic Programming, Backtracking & Greedy, Heap & Priority Queue.
templates.title: LeetCode pattern session (60 min)

templates.description:
Welcome to Module 1! This month you'll master AWS fundamentals.

Goals:
- Complete Udemy AWS SAA course sections 1-5
- Deploy a 3-tier web app manually (EC2, RDS, S3)
- Create 50+ Anki cards on AWS services
- Start LeetCode (Arrays & Hashing pattern)

Setup tasks:
- [ ] Create AWS free tier account
- [ ] Install AWS CLI and configure credentials
- [ ] Set up Terraform on your machine
- [ ] Create GitHub repo: aws-3tier-webapp
- [ ] Start LeetCode tracking spreadsheet

Resources:
- Udemy: Ultimate AWS Certified Solutions Architect Associate
- AWS Free Tier: https://aws.amazon.com/free/
- Terraform docs: https://terraform.io/docs
templates.title: Module 1: AWS Core Services — Setup & Goals
